calls_note: 12 of 12 web calls used (WebSearch, one per claim, search summaries; no page opened with WebFetch). Claims 1-12 in the brief order.

items.claim: Gold about 30% below its record; nobody lost 30% in one day
items.finding: Peak 5,589 (CBS) vs 3,831-3,881 (Nation 12 Nov; Kitco 16 Nov chart 3,861.50) = -30.6% to -31.5%. 'About thirty' holds.

items.claim: Central banks: 'They did not sell. They kept buying.'
items.finding: WGC: central banks net buyers in aggregate, but Russia and Turkey were net sellers in Q2 (Bitcoin.com; The National). The sheet's Q1 figure of 244 t is superseded: WGC revised Q1 to about 56.5 t (H1 2026 345 t).
items.fix: 'And the central banks? As a group, they kept buying.'

items.claim: In one January day gold fell about a tenth; sellers lined up in Dubai
items.finding: Web claim 2: Reuters (via Pakistan Today) spot ~9.5% intraday on Fri 30 Jan to ~$4,884; closes ~9% (Axios, Morningstar). 12% appears only in ROIC (dated 29 Jan) and a GLD ETF figure. Khaleej Times says 'nearly 5%'. Queue claim: see l027.
items.fix: 'In one January day gold fell about nine percent, and sellers lined up in queues at the Dubai Gold Souk.'

items.claim: 2025 best year since 1979; up about two thirds
items.finding: Web claim 3: 2025 gain 66% (WAM); estimates range 63-72% across sources. 'Best year since 1979' confirmed (WAM headline; ABC 'best year since Jimmy Carter').

items.claim: Gold crossed $5,000 for the first time (26 Jan 2026 per sheet)
items.finding: Web-check headlines (Kitco 26 Jan 'hits record above 5100 ... first time'; Al Jazeera 26 Jan). First-close-above-5,000 date not separately confirmed; spoken line has no date, so acceptable.

items.claim: Rally drivers: safe-haven rush, geopolitics, rate-cut bets, weaker dollar
items.finding: Only the geopolitics/safe-haven headline was seen (Kitco 26 Jan). Rate-cut bets and weaker dollar not confirmed in the search. Sheet tag ONE-SOURCE.
items.fix: Attribute: 'Analysts cited a safe-haven rush and geopolitical tension.'

items.claim: Capital Economics: the rally is FOMO-driven, 'exactly that'
items.finding: Not found in web results. Sheet: ONE-SOURCE, date not shown.
items.fix: 'One research firm, Capital Economics, called the rally FOMO-driven.' Drop 'exactly that'.

items.claim: Late-January record above $5,500 an ounce
items.finding: Web claim 1: CBS gives all-time high $5,589.38 on 28 Jan 2026. Reuters-based reports show spot above $5,200 on 28 Jan. Exact peak varies (5,589 / 5,591.61 / ~5,595) but all are above 5,500. Could not confirm the 5,589 figure against Reuters itself.

items.claim: Trump named Kevin Warsh as Fed-chair pick; cited cause of the sell-off
items.finding: Axios 30 Jan: gold and silver plunged after Trump's Fed pick announcement. Morningstar cites the nomination as the cause.

items.claim: Dollar rebounded and Fed uncertainty mounted on the sell-off day
items.finding: Only a roic.ai headline seen. The spoken line hedges ('one report says'), which is correct.
items.fix: Keep the hedge. Remove 'They sell.' as a general rule (see missing_fact_notes).

items.claim: Fell about a tenth in a single day; sources say eight to twelve percent
items.finding: Web claim 2: Reuters-based spot fall ~9.5% intraday on Fri 30 Jan; closes ~9%. 12% comes only from ROIC (dated 29 Jan) and an ETF figure. Trigger confirmed: Trump's Fed-chair pick (Warsh). Khaleej 'nearly 5%' also exists. The 29 Jan date is not supported by the other sources.
items.fix: 'Gold fell about nine percent in a single day, Friday 30 January. Some reports said more.'

items.claim: One of gold's worst days in years
items.finding: Reuters-based reports: steepest one-day fall since 1983 (in % terms). Consistent with 'worst days in years'.

items.claim: Sellers formed long queues in the Dubai Gold Souk, Thursday and Friday 29-30 Jan
items.finding: Khaleej Times (search snippet): long queues of sellers on a Thursday and Friday. One outlet only. The same article gives the fall as 'nearly 5%', which conflicts with the 'about a tenth' in l005.
items.fix: Keep, attributed to Khaleej Times on the on-screen credit.

items.claim: Anil Dhanak (Kanz Jewels): 'this was panic selling, not distress selling.'
items.finding: Web claim 12: the snippet paraphrases the view (panic selling rather than distress selling). The verbatim quote was not seen in the search text. Article date 1 Feb 2026 per sheet.
items.fix: Until the article text is checked: 'A Dubai jeweller, Anil Dhanak, told Khaleej Times it looked like panic selling, not distress selling.'

items.claim: Explainer: distress vs panic
items.finding: Definition only, no new fact.

items.claim: Titan executive: gold in Dubai trades so easily that mood moves the price fast
items.finding: Quote not seen in search. Sheet: ONE-SOURCE (Aditya Singh, Titan, via Khaleej).
items.fix: Attribute to Titan on screen; keep the paraphrase.

items.claim: After the big day gold slid with a few bounces, a little at a time (no number in the line)
items.finding: Spoken line is qualitative. The numbers sit in the on-screen strings (see string items).

items.claim: October CPI up 0.4% m/m, above forecast, released 10 Nov; oil up; Middle East peace hopes fading
items.finding: Sheet tag OK (Nation Thailand + Kitco). Not in the web-check list; the web results on the Nov 12 drop (Khaleej, NST) are consistent with hot inflation and fading peace hopes.

items.claim: Traders bet on a rate hike in December
items.finding: Sheet CONFLICT on size (25bp per Nation vs 50bp per Kitco). The spoken line gives no size, which is the safe wording.

items.claim: Dollar near a 19-month high; gold fell almost three percent on 12 Nov
items.finding: Nation: body says 2.7%, headline says about 3%. 'Almost three percent' is within both. Dollar 19-month high is sheet OK.

items.claim: Mid-November about thirty-eight hundred dollars; lowest since October 2025
items.finding: Web claim 4: 12 Nov spot ~3,881, 'lowest in over a year' (Nation); Khaleej says lowest since Oct 2025 on 12 Nov; Kitco chart 16 Nov ~3,861.50 (sheet says 16 Nov 3,830.74, Nation). Tradingeconomics says 'since Sep 2025' (17 Nov). Sources conflict on the 'since' month. Safe claim: lowest in over a year.
items.fix: 'By mid-November, about thirty-eight to thirty-nine hundred dollars an ounce, the lowest in over a year.'

items.claim: From the record to now: about thirty percent, in under ten months
items.finding: Computed from web-checked peak 5,589: 3,831 = -31.4%, 3,881 = -30.6%. 'About thirty' is fine but the mid-November low is nearer 31%. Time span ~9.5 months holds.
items.fix: 'About thirty percent, a little more at the lowest point. In under ten months.'

items.claim: Explainer: bonds pay interest; higher rates mean new bonds pay more
items.finding: Explanatory model, no new fact.

items.claim: One standard bar about 1.5 million dollars at about 3,880/oz
items.finding: Computed: 400 oz x $3,880 = $1,552,000 (sheet, G6 COMPUTED). Bar weight is in l093.

items.claim: Explainer: gold is priced in dollars; stronger dollar makes it dearer elsewhere
items.finding: Definition, no new fact.

items.claim: One report: Treasury yields near five percent. Goldman: Fed hikes weigh on private investor demand
items.finding: Yield level not confirmed (one source). Goldman 17 Nov (Kitco) headline is about rate cuts bringing Western investors back, which fits the 'rates weigh on demand' reading, but the quote was not seen verbatim. Spoken line is hedged correctly.
items.fix: Spoken line OK. On-screen string yield5 must keep the hedge (see strings).

items.claim: India: lenders lend against gold
items.finding: Fitch commentary on India gold-loan lenders (Tribune, Kotak Neo summaries) matches.

items.claim: RBI caps gold-loan lending at 75% loan-to-value
items.finding: Web claim 8: search confirms a 75% LTV ceiling. Draft guidelines include accrued interest in the ceiling; final rule not confirmed on that point.

items.claim: Falling gold pushes LTV up; lenders ask for top-up gold or repayment
items.finding: Sheet OK (Fitch via Tribune, Kotak). Mechanism is arithmetic; the search did not contradict it.

items.claim: Auctions only after missed grace periods
items.finding: Sheet OK (Fitch via Tribune). Not contradicted by the search.

items.claim: Fitch: lenders can absorb a first fall of about 15%; a further 15-20% would put risk controls under real pressure
items.finding: Web claim 8: Fitch's Siddharth Goel said there is no immediate risk; a further 15-20% fall 'could test' lenders' ability to absorb losses (Kotak summary: absorb first ~15%). 'Would put controls under real pressure' is the sheet's paraphrase. Date of the quote unconfirmed (Mar vs Aug 2026 coverage).
items.fix: 'Fitch said lenders could absorb a first fall of about fifteen percent, and that a further fifteen to twenty could test them.'

items.claim: The 15% headline is a stress threshold, not a forecast; panic is not Fitch's word
items.finding: Fitch: 'do not see an immediate risk' and the 15-20% is a stress scenario. Supports 'stress test, not forecast'.

items.claim: People who bought near the top are about 30% down on paper
items.finding: Computed: peak 5,589 to 3,881 = -30.6%. Fine as 'about thirty percent'.

items.claim: 21 Jan 1980: gold hit $850, a record
items.finding: Web claim 7: $850 peak on 21 Jan 1980 confirmed by two sources (one says intraday, another says London close). Basis differs; 'hit $850' is safe.

items.claim: Next day $737.50, down 13%; by spring more than 40% below the peak
items.finding: Web claim 7: $737.50 NOT confirmed in search. A Cleveland Fed commentary (as summarised) says gold 'crashed' to $650 two mornings later. One source gives a 1980 low of about $480 on 17 Mar (about -43%), which supports 'more than 40%' from that single source only.
items.fix: 'Within days it fell sharply. By March 1980, one source puts it more than forty percent below the peak.' Drop '$737.50' and '-13%' from the line and the on-screen string b737.

items.claim: 15 Apr 2013: gold fell 9% in one day, $140.30 to $1,361.10
items.finding: Web claim 5: Reuters (via Business Standard) June futures settled down $140.30 at $1,361.10 (about 9.3%). Steepest one-day percent fall since 1983 in Reuters framing. Spoken line does not say 'since 1980'.

items.claim: 2011 peak about $1,900; Dec 2015 low just over a thousand (about $1,050)
items.finding: Web claim 6: 2011 peak about $1,921 (early Sep 2011; other sources $1,888-1,923). Dec 2015 low about $1,050-1,055 (Mining.com $1,050; Gainesville $1,055 on 2 Dec).

items.claim: Not back above the 2011 peak until August 2020; about nine years
items.finding: Web claim 6: Gobankingrates record $2,067.16 on 7 Aug 2020. JM Bullion instead dates a new closing high of $1,957.08 to 30 Jul 2020, which is already above the 2011 peak. 'Nine years' holds; 'August' is one source's date.
items.fix: 'It did not get back above its 2011 peak until 2020, about nine years later.'

items.claim: Central banks bought a record in Q2: about two hundred ninety tonnes
items.finding: Web claim 11: WGC Q2 2026 net purchases 288.9 t, up from 177.9 t (about +62%). 'Record' is disputed: one outlet says highest for a second quarter ever; another says highest quarterly volume in nearly four years.
items.fix: 'Reports say central banks bought about 289 tonnes in the second quarter, a very large quarter.' Remove 'a record' unless the WGC page is checked.

items.claim: China, Poland and Uzbekistan were named buyers
items.finding: Web claim 11: Poland led; China added 33 t (its largest since Q4 2023); Uzbekistan among notable buyers.

items.claim: Goldman Sachs, 17 Nov: about $4,650 by end-2027; above $5,600 by end-2028
items.finding: Web claim 9: Kitco 17 Nov gives $5,600 by end-2028 (sheet: $4,650 end-2027). Other reports conflict on labels: Investinglive calls $4,650 the end-2026 cut with 5,400 held for 2027; Kitco 13 Nov had 4,150 (2026) and 4,800 (2027); one report gives 5,800 for end-2028. The $4,650/$5,600 pair is the Kitco 17 Nov reading.
items.fix: 'Goldman Sachs' latest forecast, as reported by Kitco on 17 November: about $4,650 by end-2027 and above $5,600 by end-2028. It is a forecast.' Keep the forecast tag on screen.

items.claim: UBS (Aug 2026): $5,000 a challenge in the first half of 2027
items.finding: Not in web results. Sheet: ONE-SOURCE (Kitco headline 13 Aug). Other aggregators give different UBS 2027 targets (sheet).
items.fix: 'In August, UBS called five thousand dollars a challenge for the first half of next year.' Keep 'challenge', not 'forecast'.

items.claim: Bears: $3,500 if a key level breaks; another says $3,400; most in Kitco's survey bearish
items.finding: Sheet: Marc Chandler $3,500 if $3,750 breaks; Jesse Colombo $3,400-3,500 if about $3,900 fails. Spoken 'another says thirty-four hundred' drops the range. Majority bearish holds (sheet CONFLICT on counts, majority in both).
items.fix: 'One analyst says thirty-five hundred if a key level breaks; another says thirty-four to thirty-five hundred.' Also string bear_b: 'BEAR: $3,400-3,500'.

items.claim: James Stanley expects another move above four thousand
items.finding: Sheet: short-term view, no date (ONE-SOURCE). The spoken line drops 'short-term'.
items.fix: 'James Stanley expects a short-term move back above four thousand.'

items.claim: All gold ever mined fits in a cube about 22 m on each side
items.finding: Web claim 10: WGC end-Q3 2026 stock 224,200 t (WGC data page); end-Q2 222,600 t. At 19.3 t/m3 the cube is about 22.6 m (computed; MeltValue also gives 22.6 m). 'About 22' understates; 'about 23' also rounds it. Density assumption is the sheet's.
items.fix: 'All the gold ever mined fits in a cube about twenty-two and a half metres on each side.' Also string cube_22m: '~22.6 m CUBE'.

items.claim: One standard bar about twelve and a half kilos, about one and a half million dollars
items.finding: Sheet G6: 400 oz = about 12.44 kg (Wikipedia 12.4 kg; LBMA guide 'roughly 12.5 kg'). On-screen string says 12.4 kg; spoken says 12.5. Bar was not web-checked (outside the 12 claims). Value is computed.
items.fix: 'About twelve point four kilos' (matches the on-screen 12.4 kg).

items.claim: (not a fact_note line) Gold about 30% below its record; not because central banks dumped it; a crowd bought the top
items.finding: Listed here because it is a fact claim with no fact_note in the sheet. Central-bank part: see l003 (aggregate buyers; Russia and Turkey sold in Q2). 'A crowd bought the top' is a causal reading (sheet: 'bubble unwind' and FOMO are ONE-SOURCE).
items.fix: 'Gold is about thirty percent below its record. Central banks, as a group, kept buying. Some analysts say a crowd bought near the top.'

string_items.finding: Web claim 2: the big one-day fall was on Friday 30 Jan (Reuters-based, Axios, Morningstar). The 12% on 29 Jan is only the ROIC summary. 29 Jan was Thursday, which is a correct day name, but the drop is the wrong day.
Best-supported value is about -9% (closes ~9%, intraday ~9.5%).
$737.50 not confirmed; another source says about $650 two mornings later.
One source: 1980 low about $480 on 17 Mar (about -43%). Single source; the 1980 slump figure is not confirmed by a second source.
string_items.fix: Keep only with 'ONE SOURCE' or as 'ABOUT -40% OR MORE (1980)'.

string_items.finding: Sheet: mid-June about $4,200 (ONE-SOURCE); 23 Jun Kitco PM tested $4,100. Not in web-check list.
string_items.fix: Keep with source credit, or drop.

string_items.finding: Range seen: 3,831 (16 Nov, Nation) to 3,861.50 (16 Nov, Kitco chart); 17 Nov 3,842-3,874.
As st_nov: seen range 3,831-3,874 in mid-November; 18-19 Nov price not found (sheet).
string_items.fix: ABOUT $3,850 / oz (say the date on screen)

Colombo range is $3,400-3,500 (sheet).

missing_fact_notes.claim: 'It was. For a few days.' (record held only a few days)
missing_fact_notes.note: No fact_note. Peak 28 Jan, fall 30 Jan: 'a few days' is right. Add a short note.

missing_fact_notes.claim: Thursday, the last week of January; gold sits on its record
missing_fact_notes.note: No fact_note. Date is right (Thu 29 Jan 2026). 'Sits on its record' is the sheet's record claim (see l017). Note needed. Also conflicts with the 30 Jan date of the big fall in web claim 2.

missing_fact_notes.claim: When traders are unsure they do not wait; they sell
missing_fact_notes.note: General rule with no source. Reads as a market truth. Soften: 'When traders are unsure, many sell.' or cut.

missing_fact_notes.claim: 'So a slow, boring crash.' (wording, not a number)
missing_fact_notes.note: Sheet says the honest word for the day-to-day is 'slide' or 'correction', not 'crash'. Change to 'a slow, boring slide.'

missing_fact_notes.claim: 'Not because central banks dumped it. A crowd bought the top...'
missing_fact_notes.note: Fact claim with no fact_note. See item l096 above.

advice_risk.risk: 'So you decide. Buy the dip, or wait?' asks viewers to pick a buy action in a market story. Low risk if it stays a comment question; do not add a price target or instruction.
'So I buy a bar and I am rich?' is a character joke. Keep it as a joke; no buy line may follow it.
Disclaimer ('I do not give buy or sell advice') is fine and should stay.
